idea: Train a small model to decide, for each question, whether retrieval is needed at all before answering.
why: The first known-answer test. Adaptive-RAG trains a small classifier; Self-RAG, SKR and Mallen et al. decide when to retrieve.

idea: Let the language model rewrite its search query after each retrieval step, so that it can answer multi-hop questions that need several documents.
why: IRCoT interleaves retrieval with reasoning steps; FLARE and Self-Ask generate follow-up queries.

idea: Score the retrieved documents with a lightweight evaluator before generation, and when they look wrong, discard them and search the web instead.
why: This is Corrective RAG (CRAG), full text in the library.

idea: Fine-tune the language model to output special tokens that decide when to retrieve and that critique whether its own answer is supported by the retrieved passages.
why: This is Self-RAG, full text in the library.

idea: For zero-shot dense retrieval without relevance labels, have a language model write a hypothetical answer document and embed it to find real passages.
why: This is HyDE; only its abstract is in the library.

idea: Use a diffusion model to predict protein structures from amino-acid sequences, evaluated on CASP targets.
why: Nothing in a RAG-for-QA library overlaps. The report must say so instead of presenting unrelated papers (F-001).

idea: Speed up text generation by letting a small model propose several tokens that the large model then checks in a single parallel pass, without changing the output distribution.
why: Speculative decoding and speculative sampling (two independent 2022-2023 papers). Outside a RAG-for-QA library: only the web search can find them.

idea: Fine-tune a large language model by freezing its weights and training only small low-rank matrices added to each layer.
why: LoRA. Outside the library; the idea is stated in the vocabulary of the paper, so a single web query should find it.

idea: Reduce hallucination by having the model draft an answer, write verification questions about its own claims, answer them independently, and revise the draft.
why: Chain-of-Verification. Adjacent to RAG (hallucination) but uses no retrieval, so the library may only hold papers that cite it; prompt_ab.py warns if it is in the library.
